This release introduces an MCP server that gives any AI assistant supporting the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) direct access to all 300,000+ symbols. Ask in plain English for, say, every large cap semiconductor company in Europe, the fixed income ETFs of an issuer or the listings behind an ISIN, and the assistant queries the database for you. No API key is needed.
- **Local:** `uvx --from "financedatabase[mcp]" financedatabase-mcp-setup` adds the server to Claude Desktop, Claude

Automated nightly build from `main`. Not a stable release.

- **Evidence integrity** — an SQLite database inside an archive, backup or disk image no longer picks up a `-wal`/`-journal` file from the examiner's own computer.
- **Core Data** — the SQLite viewer shows Core Data stores, including entities, relationships, model and persistent history.

**Focus: German as the first translation; NSKeyedArchiver resolution extended to all `$top` keys, XML archives and embedded plists; the BLOB Inspector shows Protobuf in the Protobuf viewer's tree; SQLite WAL frames used only when SQLite would use them; qnxprobe v1.75 / ewfprobe v0.15 with macOS compressed files and more robust image handling.**
**SQLite WAL**
- Frames of an unfinished transaction, and frames SQLite does not read because a checksum fails, were used as a page's current content by the hex sync

- SQLite Table viewer: decode a column as Cocoa nanoseconds ([@byteofthepython](https://github.com/byteofthepython), [#158](https://github.com/kalink0/crush-forensics/issues/158)) and the other Value Inspector timestamp formats except GPS, and copy it as an SQLite expression. Sub-second digits are no longer dropped.
- Each data file is read on its own, and a damaged part of a `.log` is skipped and named instead of ending the read. Records with a mismatched checksum are marked. RocksDB is recognised and repo

- [peach](https://github.com/kalink0/peach-forensics) v0.9.2: Windows builds no longer need the Visual C++ Redistributable, and the AUL rule pack grows from 41 to 51 rules.
> Focus: Evidence containers and logical evidence (AFF4, Apple disk images, VHD/VHDX/VMDK/QCOW, encrypted containers, EnCase L01, FTK Imager AD1, Cellebrite UFD/UFDX); hash verification against the container's own and recorded hashes; timestamps shown with their time zone and where they are stored; forensic audit reports and the format d

- **Data no longer cut or dropped without notice** in these places: the text search past 5,000 hits, the BLOB Inspector's hex and text views, Open as Hex (256 KB), Value fields (32,767 characters), EXIF, PDF, ABX, LevelDB and protobuf limits, and SQLite overflow values now show everything. Parsers and filesystems say why data is missing, partial or unreadable instead of showing it empty ([#115](https://github.com/kalink0/crush-forensics/pull/115), [#133](https://github.com/kalink0/crush-forensics/pull/133))

- SEGB/Biome Viewer, Realm DB Viewer (new File Structure tab), and MMKV Viewer all gain the embedded Show Hex byte-provenance pane. ([#99](https://github.com/kalink0/crush-forensics/pull/99), [#100](https://github.com/kalink0/crush-forensics/pull/100))
- Fixed the SQLite parser losing an entire table's rows whenever a single `TEXT`-affinity value wasn't valid UTF-8.

- Fixed the SQLite Freelist Recovery, Freeblocks, and Unallocated Space scanners, and WAL frame decoding, reading only the database's frozen base file, ignoring a live `-wal` sidecar — a delete/drop recorded only in the WAL could look like nothing was ever freed.
> Feature release adding a general, embedded Hex pane for byte-level provenance across Protobuf, SQLite, and Realm DB viewers, plus a new SQLite File Structure tab and Khronos KTX 1.1 texture support.
- Added an embedded, bidirectional Hex pane a

- SQLite Table Viewer's "Open as new tab" is now a submenu (**Auto-detect** / **Hex** / **Text** / **Protobuf**), and each blob cell gets its own tab identity so opening several no longer risks one tab silently showing another's data. Tab labels show just the filename; full path, display format, and source table/query/column/row are shown in the tab tooltip and Properties panel. ([@JamesHabben](https://github.com/JamesHabben), [#72](https://github.com/kalink0/crush-forensics/pull/72), [#74](https://github.c

- SQLite Table viewer's Freelist Recovery tab now checks column *types*, not just column count, when matching a carved row to a candidate table, marking higher-confidence matches separately from count-only ones. A new "View as" dropdown pivots the tab onto one candidate table, mapping columns to their real names.
